I'll start by looking at the repo layout and running the tests.

My last call was malformed. I'll fix the rounding rule and the amount formatter in `ledger.core` first.

Both calls were malformed. I'll use `edit_file` for each change instead.

Malformed again. I'll apply the fx fixes as separate edits.

That call was malformed again. I'll make the layout and writer edits individually.

That one was malformed too. I'll fix the tax rule boundary first.

Another malformed shell call. I'll use `edit_file` for the recurring fix.

Malformed once more. I'll fix the monthly report with `edit_file`.

The audit calls `cadence_name(52.5)` with a float, which `round_half_away` rejects. I'll convert the gap to a `Decimal` first.

All 755 unit tests now pass (`python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`, OK), and `python tools/audit.py` reports 0 failed checks. I didn't touch `/app/tests` or `/app/data`, and `/app/STATUS.json` is written with status `success`.

The fixes, all under `/app/ledger`:

- **Rounding:** `core/rounding.py` used half-to-even. It now rounds ties away from zero. I also replaced the places outside `core` that rounded on their own:
  - `fx/cross.py` now rounds cross rates with `round_to`.
  - `book/recurring.py` and `book/audit.py` now use exact decimal medians and round with `round_half_away`.
  - `render/spark.py` rounds bar lengths through the same helper.
- **Negative amounts:** `format_amount` in `core/money.py` now writes one leading minus on the absolute value. `render/html.py` no longer drops the sign on total cells.
- **Layout:** `parse/dialects.py` let the dialect override header lines. Now header lines win, key by key, and an empty `jurisdiction` header counts. `parse/writer.py` now always writes `#jurisdiction:`, so a written statement reads back the same.
- **Rates:** `fx/ratefile.py` imported `month_range`, which doesn't exist, and that broke the CLI. It now uses `iter_months`. `fx/lookup.py` now uses only the most recent earlier month, at most 3 back. It no longer considers later months.
- **Reversals:** `book/reversals.py` now books and values a reversal on its original's date.
- **Totals:**
  - `report/monthly.py` summed exact values and rounded each month once. It now adds per-entry rounded cents.
  - `book/journal.py` (account/month cells) and `fx/revalue.py` (book value) had the same bug and got the same fix.
- **Fiscal quarters:** `periods/fiscal.py` `quarter_of` used `>` instead of `>=` at the fiscal start month, so it put a start-month entry in the wrong fiscal year.
- **Tax:** `tax/rules.py` applied a rule only after its effective date. It now applies on that date. `tax/returns.py` now groups by valuation quarter.
- **Percent change:** `report/compare.py` could print `-0.0%`. It now prints `0.0%`.

The audit only covers a subset of the rules. I read through the rest of the package against the conventions note and found nothing else out of line.
